clues: This city is centered on a river, in the south-central part of its small northern state. Fish once thronged the river's rapids in spring.
Winters here are long, cold, and snowy, and spring and fall pass quickly. Summers are warm, and at times humid.
In 1808, this town was named the seat of state rule. Its state house, built in 1819, is still used by lawmakers in the same rooms.
A schoolteacher from this city flew into space in 1986. She was picked to teach lessons from orbit, and the whole nation mourned when her shuttle was lost.
New Hampshire's governor works in this town. Its lawmakers meet in the old state house by the river.
